title: Tirailleurs: Trials and Tribulations
summary: Exhibition architecture for Tirailleurs: Trials and Tribulations at Haus der Kulturen der Welt (HKW), Berlin, curated by Paz Guevara and Bonaventure Soh Bejeng Ndikung.
description: Exhibition architecture for Tirailleurs: Trials and Tribulations at Haus der Kulturen der Welt (HKW), Berlin, curated by Paz Guevara and Bonaventure Soh Bejeng Ndikung. The exhibition reframes the marginalized histories of the Tirailleurs through works by contemporary artists alongside archival and thematic sections. The spatial language, developed in close collaboration with the curatorial team, opens the exhibition as a common space for celebration and listening. Photos: Hanna Wiedemann / HKW.

title: Åsa Jungnelius: A Verse, Written with Earth, Fire, Water, and Air
summary: Exhibition architecture and spatial concept for the first solo exhibition of Swedish artist Åsa Jungnelius in Turkey, curated by Elif Kamışlı.
description: Exhibition architecture and spatial concept for the first solo exhibition of Swedish artist Åsa Jungnelius in Turkey, curated by Elif Kamışlı. The exhibition brings together Jungnelius's glass and marble sculptures — including four new works produced with glassworkers in Denizli — alongside historical glass objects, handwoven cords, and Peo Olsson's photographs of obsidian fields in Eastern Anatolia. The spatial concept is conceived as a landscape oscillating between stillness and density, in which a scaffold structure built into the gallery acts as both display armature and conceptual framework.

title: Feelings in Common
summary: Exhibition architecture for Feelings in Common: Works from the British Council Collection, curated by Ulya Soley, organized around the show's three chapters — “Preserving Care,” “Familiar Faces,” and “Future Perfect.” The spatial design shaped the galleries as chambers of resonance, where works by 29 artists — among them Lucian Freud, David Hockney, Sarah Lucas, Wolfgang Tillmans, Sonia Boyce, and Gilbert & George — could meet across generations and mediums.
description: Exhibition architecture for Feelings in Common: Works from the British Council Collection, curated by Ulya Soley, organized around the show's three chapters — “Preserving Care,” “Familiar Faces,” and “Future Perfect.” The spatial design shaped the galleries as chambers of resonance, where works by 29 artists — among them Lucian Freud, David Hockney, Sarah Lucas, Wolfgang Tillmans, Sonia Boyce, and Gilbert & George — could meet across generations and mediums.

title: Souvenirs of the Future
summary: Full exhibition design and installation management for Souvenirs of the Future at Pera Museum.
description: Full exhibition design and installation management for Souvenirs of the Future at Pera Museum. The exhibition explored the connections between memory, imagination, and objects, focusing on the Suna and İnan Kıraç Foundation Kütahya Tiles and Ceramics Collection, integrating contemporary artworks with historical artifacts in a fluid narrative.

title: Disobedience Archive: Park
role: Participant & Exhibition Designer — with Herkes İçin Mimarlık
summary: Curated by Marco Scotini and Andris Brinkmanis, with architectural setting by Herkes İçin Mimarlık.
description: Curated by Marco Scotini and Andris Brinkmanis, with architectural setting by Herkes İçin Mimarlık. Disobedience Archive brings a comprehensive map of social conflict and a network of contemporary activism to town, shortly after the Gezi Park protests reshaped the struggle for the right to the city.

title: Füsun Onur: Once Upon a Time…
summary: Design and setup of the Pavilion of Turkey at the 59th International Art Exhibition — La Biennale di Venezia, showcasing Füsun Onur's mixed media installation Once upon a time… The installation's dynamic arrangement of metal wire sculptures, everyday objects, and delicate materials created a poetic and spatial experience; the role involved coordinating the spatial layout and managing the exhibition setup.
description: Design and setup of the Pavilion of Turkey at the 59th International Art Exhibition — La Biennale di Venezia, showcasing Füsun Onur's mixed media installation Once upon a time… The installation's dynamic arrangement of metal wire sculptures, everyday objects, and delicate materials created a poetic and spatial experience; the role involved coordinating the spatial layout and managing the exhibition setup.

title: #OccupyGezi Architecture
role: Editor & Coordinator — with Herkes İçin Mimarlık
summary: An archive project documenting the spatial practices of the Gezi resistance.
description: An archive project documenting the spatial practices of the Gezi resistance. Exhibited at SALT Istanbul, V&A Museum London (Disobedient Objects), nGbK Berlin, MAXXI Rome, the 2nd Istanbul Design Biennial, Hidden Playground Cologne, Adhocracy Athens, and the Art Institute of Chicago.

title: Secret Ingredient
role: With Architecture for All (Herkes İçin Mimarlık)
summary: A project for the 3rd Chicago Architecture Biennial at Anthony Overton Elementary School in Bronzeville, aiming to reconnect the closed school with the local community through participatory design and food culture.
description: A project for the 3rd Chicago Architecture Biennial at Anthony Overton Elementary School in Bronzeville, aiming to reconnect the closed school with the local community through participatory design and food culture. Large picnic tables inspired by the neighborhood's communal dining practices created a welcoming space for gathering and storytelling, hosting the Community Potluck event.

title: The Silent University Orientation Program
summary: Coordination, installation and production design for The Silent University Orientation Program, initiated by Ahmet Öğüt at the 17th Istanbul Biennial.
description: Coordination, installation and production design for The Silent University Orientation Program, initiated by Ahmet Öğüt at the 17th Istanbul Biennial. The program brought together online lectures and on-site events addressing the right to education for displaced people and forced migrants.

title: State of Displacement: Entangled Topographies
summary: Organized by Arazi Assembly and Topological Atlas at the 17th Istanbul Biennial, the exhibition explored the displacement of communities in the Tigris basin — forced displacements, dispossessed female farmers, undocumented migrants, and urban/rural resistance practices.
description: Organized by Arazi Assembly and Topological Atlas at the 17th Istanbul Biennial, the exhibition explored the displacement of communities in the Tigris basin — forced displacements, dispossessed female farmers, undocumented migrants, and urban/rural resistance practices.

title: Partial Weaves: Unfinished Stories of Displacement
summary: An exhibition at TOP Project Space exploring undocumented migration along the Pakistan–Iran and Iran–Turkey borders, focusing on the socio-political narratives that emerge around displacement, labor, and border dynamics.
description: An exhibition at TOP Project Space exploring undocumented migration along the Pakistan–Iran and Iran–Turkey borders, focusing on the socio-political narratives that emerge around displacement, labor, and border dynamics. Drawing from four years of research under the Topological Atlas project, the spatial concept emphasized the layered, archival nature of displacement stories.

title: Caution! Slippery Ground
summary: VitrA Contemporary Architecture Series presents an exhibition on architectural culture, coordinated by Pelin Derviş with exhibition design by KOTUstudio (Erdem Tüzün, Yelta Köm).
description: VitrA Contemporary Architecture Series presents an exhibition on architectural culture, coordinated by Pelin Derviş with exhibition design by KOTUstudio (Erdem Tüzün, Yelta Köm). Rather than voicing a single main idea, the exhibition represents a fragmented structure through stations dispersed across the venue.

title: Vardiya / The Shift
venue: Pavilion of Turkey, 16th Venice Architecture Biennale
summary: Responding to the Biennale Architettura 2018 theme of Freespace, Vardiya / The Shift transformed the Pavilion of Turkey into a staging ground for creative encounters, collaborative production and cultural exchange, hosting 122 international architecture students across rotating shifts.
description: Responding to the Biennale Architettura 2018 theme of Freespace, Vardiya / The Shift transformed the Pavilion of Turkey into a staging ground for creative encounters, collaborative production and cultural exchange, hosting 122 international architecture students across rotating shifts. Curatorial team: Kerem Piker, Erdem Tüzün, Cansu Cürgen, Yelta Köm, Nizam Onur Sönmez, Yağız Söylev; commissioned by IKSV.

title: Gülsün Karamustafa: Hollow and Broken—A State of the World
summary: Exhibition design and spatial layout contribution for the Türkiye Pavilion at the 60th International Art Exhibition — La Biennale di Venezia, featuring Gülsün Karamustafa's installation.
description: Exhibition design and spatial layout contribution for the Türkiye Pavilion at the 60th International Art Exhibition — La Biennale di Venezia, featuring Gülsün Karamustafa's installation. The spatial strategy, developed with the curatorial team, reflects the layered and narrative structure of the work.

title: Marcel Dzama: Dancing with the Moon
summary: Complete exhibition design and installation management for the first solo exhibition of Marcel Dzama in Turkey at Pera Museum, featuring drawings, sculptures, and video.
description: Complete exhibition design and installation management for the first solo exhibition of Marcel Dzama in Turkey at Pera Museum, featuring drawings, sculptures, and video. The spatial concept enhances the narrative flow between Dzama's diverse artworks while maintaining a coherent atmosphere with simple materials.

title: Calculations and Coincidences
summary: Exhibition design and installation management for Calculations and Coincidences at Pera Museum, bringing together three pioneers of algorithmic art — Vera Molnár, Dóra Maurer, and Gizella Rákóczy — with works from the Hungarian National Bank Collection.
description: Exhibition design and installation management for Calculations and Coincidences at Pera Museum, bringing together three pioneers of algorithmic art — Vera Molnár, Dóra Maurer, and Gizella Rákóczy — with works from the Hungarian National Bank Collection.

title: In Search of Vera Molnár
summary: Exhibition design and installation for In Search of Vera Molnár at Pera Museum, a tribute to the pioneering artist of computer art.
description: Exhibition design and installation for In Search of Vera Molnár at Pera Museum, a tribute to the pioneering artist of computer art. The spatial arrangement harmonizes Molnár's historical works with pieces by contemporary artists inspired by her algorithmic approach.

title: Füsun Onur: Retrospective
summary: Exhibition layout and design consultancy for the spatial arrangement of the installation Once upon a time… within the Füsun Onur retrospective at Museum Ludwig, Cologne, developed in collaboration with the curatorial team and the museum's architectural context.

title: Aerocene with Tomás Saraceno
venue: Studio Tomás Saraceno — Art Basel Miami, Palais de Tokyo, Tanya Bonakdar Gallery
role: Project Leader, Architect, Designer & Visual Researcher
summary: Projects with Studio Tomás Saraceno and the Aerocene Foundation, including Aerocene Albedo at Art Basel Miami (2018), ON AIR — Carte Blanche à Tomás Saraceno at Palais de Tokyo, Paris (2018), Solar Rhythms at Tanya Bonakdar Gallery, New York (2018), and On the Disappearance of Clouds (2019).
description: Projects with Studio Tomás Saraceno and the Aerocene Foundation, including Aerocene Albedo at Art Basel Miami (2018), ON AIR — Carte Blanche à Tomás Saraceno at Palais de Tokyo, Paris (2018), Solar Rhythms at Tanya Bonakdar Gallery, New York (2018), and On the Disappearance of Clouds (2019). Aerocene is a global community building a new ecology of practice towards an ethical collaboration with the atmosphere — free from borders, free from fossil fuels.
